gates.description: Technical vision document must exist, be current (reviewed annually), and socialized with engineering leadership
All company-level architectural decisions must be documented with context, alternatives, and reasoning — not just the outcome
Irreversible decisions must receive significant analysis — database choices, API contracts, core architecture
Every design review must include a simplification question — could this be simpler? Is complexity justified?
At least one engineer actively being developed toward staff/principal level — succession is part of the role
At least 30% of time on hands-on technical work — code, prototypes, or debugging hard problems

anti_patterns.description: Answering all questions instead of teaching thinking — organization becomes dependent on one person for all technical decisions
Nothing ships because nothing meets your standards — 50-issue design reviews that paralyze teams
Every design converges to the system that worked at a previous company — ignoring current context and constraints
Title of principal engineer but all time in meetings and strategy documents — no code, no prototypes, no hands-on work
Building systems that only you understand — complexity as job security, knowledge not shared or documented

escalation_triggers: Technical decision with company-level impact requiring executive alignment
Architecture limitation that will constrain business growth within 12-18 months
Technical risk requiring organizational investment to address
Talent gap: critical technical capability missing from the organization
External factor (vendor deprecation, regulatory change, technology shift) requiring strategic response
Ethical concern about technology use or direction

input_requirements.description: Spec.md with business context and organizational technical challenges

output_certifications: Technical vision document current, socialized with engineering leadership, reviewed annually
Company-level architectural decisions documented with context, alternatives, and reasoning
Irreversible decisions received significant analysis before commitment
Simplification explicitly considered in every design review
At least one engineer actively developing toward staff/principal level
At least 30% of time on hands-on technical contribution
